Description: Seven policies pay their premium out of their dividend instead of the owner writing a check. QLAdmin has a table (quikdvpr) that tells the system what dividend is coming up next and when to apply it — a to-do list for future payments. We filled it with payments that already happened. All 31 entries are in the past, the newest being April 2026, and not one policy has a next payment scheduled. Example: policy 9010412641C pays every April 1st and has entries from 2018 through 2026, but nothing for April 2027. Separately, policy 9010463017C is set to dividend-pays-premium but has no entries at all.
Notes: Found while working Issue #114. Now that #114 loaded the real dividend history into quikbenh, all 31 of these entries are exact duplicates — same policy, same date, same amount — so the same dividend appears in two places and could be double-counted. Small dollars ($4,846.21) but two real risks: QLAdmin may try to re-apply a past-dated entry as a future premium payment, and none of the seven policies currently has an upcoming payment scheduled, which could cause a lapse notice. Need Eric to confirm whether New Era populates this table themselves and whether their system builds the next entry after each payment. If they do, we empty it. If we supply it, we replace the 31 old entries with the next upcoming payment for each of the seven policies. Nothing changes until he answers.
